learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will understand the concept of time in sentences and learn to use Simple Present, Present Continuous, and Simple Past tenses.]
warm_up_hook: ⏳ Time travel is real in English Grammar! We can talk about things happening right now, things that happened yesterday, and things that happen every day. Let's master the magic of Tenses!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We use the Simple Present tense for things we do every day (habits) or things that are always true. For singular subjects (He, She, It), we add '-s' or '-es' to the verb.
If an action is happening RIGHT NOW, as we speak, we use the Present Continuous tense. We make it by using (is/am/are) + action verb with an '-ing' tail!
examples_or_templates: I [am eating] an apple right now.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When an action is already finished, we use the Simple Past tense. We usually add '-ed' to the end of the action verb. But some tricky verbs change their spelling completely!
examples_or_templates: Irregular (Tricky): go -> went, eat -> ate, see -> saw

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which sentence is in the Present Continuous Tense?
❓ What is the Simple Past tense of the verb 'Go'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Add '-s' or '-es' to complete the Simple Present sentence: 'My father ________ (watch) the news every evening.'
✍️ Change the verb to Present Continuous: 'The birds _________ (fly) in the sky.'
subjective_practice.hint: Add 'are' because birds is plural, and add '-ing' to fly.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change this sentence to Simple Past tense: 'I clean my room.'
subjective_practice.hint: Clean is a regular verb. Just add '-ed' at the end!

activity_or_assignment.title: ⏰ The Time Machine Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Pick an action, like 'Eat'. Write three sentences using your time machine: 1) Every day I eat... (Simple Present) 2) Right now I am eating... (Continuous) 3) Yesterday I ate... (Simple Past).

chapter_summary: ⭐ Simple Present tells us about daily habits and facts.
⭐ Add '-s' or '-es' to the verb for singular subjects in Simple Present.
⭐ Present Continuous (is/am/are + verb-ing) tells us what is happening right now.
⭐ Simple Past tells us about finished actions, usually by adding '-ed'.
